in_text_mentions: ost common finding in the external examination was the singeing of body hair, observed in almost all cases. Lichtenberg figures, a characteristic finding of lightning strikes, were detected in 6 of the 13 cases (46.1%) (Figure 1). These figures were localized on the abdomen, chest, right arm, and left thigh. Internal examination revealed subarachnoid hemorrhage in 3 cases (23%), pulmonary hemorrhage in 2 cases, liver laceration in 1 case, and liver hemorrhage in 1 case. In the majority of the cases (53.8%, n = 7), no specific macroscopic pathological findings were found in the internal organs.

Blast injuries were found on his lips and chin, while Lichtenberg figures were present on the right side of the neck and back, and along the spinal processes.

Excluded per findings-vocabulary rule. B: Panel-specific caption B right foot in lightning-strike case report with visual small oval punctate burn consistent with punctate lightning entry burn. D: Toe burn/necrosis from lightning strike but not clearly punctate entry morphology nor fern-like Lichtenberg pattern; no vocabulary finding can be named without inventing. panels.figure_caption: Picture of the cutaneous lesion (A. torso, B. right foot, C. left ear, D. toes right foot, E. ankles, F. back).
in_text_mentions: At the emergency department, physical examination revealed burns on both feet, ankles, pubic area, torso, back, and left ear (Fig. 1). Blood analysis revealed an elevated creatine kinase (CK) level of 3700 UI/L (range 100–200 UI/L). Cerebral and cervical computed tomography (CT) scans showed no evidence of bleeding or structural injuries. The subject was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit where he remained intubated and sedated for 3 days. A tympanic membrane perforation was detected. Upon awakening on day 3, the subject exhibited paraparesis.
